issues.issue: Did the IAD err by refusing to consider post-marriage evidence of genuineness when deciding the primary purpose of the marriage?
issues.applicant_position: Post-marriage evidence of commitment is relevant to primary purpose; the IAD erred by ignoring it entirely, misreading Gill 2014 and Singh as conflicting.
issues.respondent_position: Only evidence leading up to the marriage counts for primary purpose; Sandhu supports this; Gill 2014 misstates the law.
issues.result_quote: I find the IAD’s failure to consider this evidence to render its decision unreasonable.

issues.issue: Did the IAD err by treating s. 4(1) as a disjunctive test and declining to assess whether the marriage was genuine?
issues.applicant_position: Gill 2014 and Singh are reconcilable; the IAD wrongly treated them as conflicting, so it skipped post-marriage evidence.
issues.respondent_position: Gill 2014 misstates the law; the test is disjunctive, so the IAD needed no genuineness finding once primary purpose was found.
issues.result_quote: It therefore did not engage in the analysis regarding the genuineness of the marriage, the second element of the test. In that, I find no error.

issues.issue: Are the other grounds of review argued by the applicant reviewable errors?
issues.applicant_position: Raised other grounds of review; the text does not describe them.
issues.result_quote: It is unnecessary for the Court to consider the other grounds of review argued by Mr. Lawrence.
